description: Chúng mình là NAU SPACE APPS, đội thi gồm 5 thành viên đến từ Trường Đại học Nghệ An, tham gia NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 với dự án INSIGHT'S LAST DIARY. Đội yêu thích khoa học, công nghệ, khám phá vũ trụ và đổi mới sáng tạo. Chúng mình tìm kiếm những thành viên có kỹ năng lập trình, AI, phân tích dữ liệu, thiết kế, nghiên cứu khoa học, tiếng Anh và thuyết trình. Điều quan trọng nhất là nhiệt huyết, trách nhiệm và tinh thần học hỏi!
summary: What happens after a spacecraft stops sending signals? Team NAU EXPLORERS (NS01048) developed InSight: The Last Diary from Mars, an interactive 10-chapter bilingual (English–Vietnamese) web storytelling application designed for young explorers aged 10–15. Grounded in primary NASA, JPL, and NSSDCA (ID: 2018-042A) records, our platform transforms technical mission archives into a first-person narrative told from the perspective of NASA’s retired InSight lander on Elysium Planitia. Students inspect an interactive 3D model of the lander’s instruments, explore a 3D cutaway of Mars’ crust, lumpy mantle, and liquid core, listen to amplified Martian wind and seismic waveforms, and balance limited solar power as red dust accumulates from 5,000 down to 500 Wh per sol. By turning dense archives into an accessible, browser-based STEM experience, our project demonstrates that even when space hardware falls silent, its scientific discoveries continue to advance human knowledge.
details:
OVERVIEW & HOW IT WORKS
Built as a dedicated 10-page interactive storytelling module under our broader "Abandoned But Not Forgotten" educational initiative, "InSight: The Last Diary from Mars" transforms official NASA/JPL and NSSDCA mission records into an engaging, self-paced journey for learners aged 10–15. Instead of presenting dense tables of dates and technical telemetry, the web application invites students to read and interact with the first-person mission diary of NASA's stationary InSight lander (NSSDCA ID: 2018-042A) resting at Elysium Planitia (4.502°N, 135.623°E).

The experience is structured into ten sequential chapters:
01. The Last Diary — First-person introduction with an interactive Martian horizon, drifting dust particles, and ambient Martian wind audio.
02. Meet InSight — Explains why InSight is a stationary geophysical lander with no wheels, comparing it to rolling Mars rovers.
03. The Journey to Mars — An animated 6-stage orbital and mission trajectory map tracing InSight's 485-million-km cruise from Vandenberg (May 5, 2018) alongside twin MarCO CubeSats, touchdown (November 26, 2018), and final contact (December 15, 2022).
04. The Mission — Introduces InSight's three core scientific investigations (SEIS, HP³, and RISE) with an interactive discovery check.
05. Inside My Body — A dual-view 3D hardware explorer (Three.js 3D model + official NASA PIA17358 diagram + live embedded NASA Eyes on the Solar System view) allowing learners to inspect 9 subsystems on demand.
06. The Heart of Mars — An interactive 3D planetary cutaway (Crust, Lumpy Mantle, and 1,830-km Molten Liquid Core) illustrating how seismic waves reveal internal layers.
07. Listening to the Planet — Visualizes P-waves vs. S-waves and provides 3 ear-safe amplified Martian wind and marsquake audio tracks alongside NASA/JPL's official acoustic recording.
08. The Secrets I Left Behind — Highlights major discoveries, including NASA's August 2025 Science study revealing 4-km-wide ancient asteroid impact lumps preserved inside Mars' sluggish mantle, 1,319 recorded marsquakes, fresh meteorite impacts, and crustal magnetism.
09. When the Lights Went Out — Features a before-and-after solar panel dust scrubber (Dec 2018 vs. April 2022) synced with the drop from ~5,000 Wh/sol to ~500 Wh/sol, plus an educational resource-allocation trade-off exercise and the engineering lessons from the HP³ heat probe.
10. Abandoned, But Not Forgotten — Concludes with a 3-question review quiz, a personalized 4D Explorer Mission Badge generator, and a full Reference & Transparency Ledger.

TECHNOLOGY STACK & ARCHITECTURE
- Frontend & 3D Graphics: HTML5, CSS3 (Responsive Grid, Glassmorphism, 3D CSS Perspective), JavaScript/TypeScript (React), and Three.js (WebGL) for real-time 3D lander and Martian core visualizations.
- Audio & Canvas Rendering: Web Audio API (with DynamicsCompressorNode peak normalization for comfortable listening across speakers and headphones) and HTML5 Canvas for starfield parallax and high-resolution badge generation.
- Accessibility & Localization: Instant 100% English / 100% Vietnamese language toggle, desktop edge-hover navigation, mobile horizontal swipe gestures, and touch-safe 3D controls.
- Open-Source Hosting: Version-controlled on GitHub under Apache License 2.0 ([INSERT PUBLIC GITHUB REPO URL]) and deployed publicly via Vercel (https://silent-monuments-voices-from-the-mo.vercel.app).

BENEFITS, EXPECTED IMPACT & FACTORS CONSIDERED
- Educational Impact: Removes cost, hardware, and language barriers by delivering a free browser-based STEM tool requiring zero paid accounts or VR headsets, empowering Vietnamese and global students aged 10–15 to connect spacecraft engineering with real scientific evidence.
- Interdisciplinary Creativity: Leveraging our team's background in economics and management, we translated InSight's declining solar power budget (5,000 to 500 Wh/sol) and HP³ soil penetration limits (~40 cm vs. 5 m target) into interactive lessons on scarce resource allocation and scientific resilience.
- Scientific & Representational Integrity: Every screen clearly distinguishes creative first-person narration and simplified educational diagrams ("not to scale") from verified NASA/JPL telemetry, explicitly noting acoustic speed-up factors (60x–100x) and geophysical uncertainty margins.
